verdicts.note: Men's co-residence with their own CHILDREN in England and Wales; a different co-residence.
Telehealth mattress for older adults.
Preschool outcomes of children raised in a prison nursery.

WEALTH MODIFIES the relationship between kin and women's fertility in high-income countries -- a moderator result on the extended arm's mechanism. Exposure is kin presence and support rather than the arrangement, so C.2.a's, but the heterogeneity finding matters for the extended arm's transportability.
Intergenerational co-residence as income sharing that mitigates single mothers' poverty in Japan, 67,252 observations. Arrangement as exposure, poverty as outcome.
Grandparents co-residing with grandchildren in Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam, usually with the parents also present. Care provision described, no fertility outcome.
Surgical society presidential address on medical education.
Microsimulation of complex households for European city models.

THE MARGINAL COST OF A BEDROOM in Australia, against rising multigenerational and group living and policy incentives aimed at fertility. Prices the space constraint that C.2.c owns while the arrangement is the changing quantity -- Wall 1 from the housing-economics side.

Argues the falling parent-child co-residence rate in Japan is partly an artefact of rising CHILDLESSNESS among elders, who have no co-residence option. A composition warning for any co-residence trend series -- worth carrying to §9.
Changing legal conceptions of parenthood in English law.
Population projection for Malaysian development planning.
Young children at home and menopausal hot flashes.

Care leavers as an exception to the extended-transition norm, with ACCELERATED transitions. A subpopulation whose home-leaving is externally imposed -- noted as a possible design-4 analogue, but no fertility outcome.
Young people not in education, employment or training.
Repartnering by parenthood and CHILDREN'S living arrangements, NCDS and BCS. Co-residence with one's own children.
Essay on evolutionary psychology and history.
Advice literature on parenting emerging adults.
Social networks and mental health cross-nationally.
Gay men's fatherhood in Norway.
Chapter on changing western family structures and the ageing of life transitions.
Nephrology editorial.
Book-chapter version of the second-demographic-transition assessment. D.1.a's.

'Growth in a PATRILOCAL ECONOMY: Female Schooling, Household Savings, and China's One-Child Policy'. A model in which the residence rule shapes parental investment; theory for the extended arm's largest setting.
Illinois law on stepparent childcare.
Constitutional constraints on second-parent laws.
Living arrangements of the elderly in Fiji.
No abstract; childbearing and marital histories and women's retirement.
No abstract; food intake among Moroccan oasis women.
Sex-selective abortion in Azerbaijan; 'boomerang effect' is the policy metaphor. D.2.c's.
Care provision for ageing baby boomers.
Stem-family prevalence compared across two Irish counties by farm size. Pre-modern; A.7's.
Emotional closeness and genetic relatedness against RECEIVING CHILD CARE from parents and parents-in-law. Childcare receipt as outcome.
Reference entry 'Family as Institution', no abstract.
No abstract; transition from paediatric to adult cystic fibrosis services.
Japanese panel analysis of the probability of childbirth and the two-child norm. Whether co-residence is among the tracked conditions is not visible in the truncated abstract; trace.
Sequence analysis of pathways to adulthood in URUGUAY from two national youth surveys. Latin American setting; sequence method.
Book review of 'Spatial Mobility, Migration, and Living Arrangements'; no abstract. The volume itself may be worth tracing.
Household change across four Chinese censuses 1982-2010: shrinking size, simplifying structure. Exposure trend with census-scale data in the extended arm's key setting.

Inter-generational co-residence and women's WORK AND LEISURE TIME in Egypt, framed by the expectation that women will spend longer co-residing with ageing in-laws. The arrangement is the exposure and the outcome is time use.
Socioeconomic differences in parental support to adult children.
Past-union children, resident and nonresident, against couple childbearing intentions. Co-residence with one's own children.
Latent class and latent transition analysis of education, LEAVING HOME, work, relationships and PARENTING at ages 20 and 29 in an Australian cohort. The whole sequence in one longitudinal design.
Parental stress in Prader-Willi syndrome.

Declining family size and the lost benefits of within-household sharing, arguing projections ignore household formation. The economies-of-scale argument that makes co-residence attractive -- the mechanism running the other way from A.23's.

'Adult attainment projects' as a bundle of labour force participation, RESIDENTIAL INDEPENDENCE, marriage, PARENTHOOD and homeownership, by class, 1980-2010. Treats the sequence as one object; class gradient is what it estimates.

Microsimulation showing how fertility, marriage and mortality CONSTRAIN co-residence patterns in historic Eastern Europe. The demographic-availability constraint on the arrangement -- a confound the chapter's trend records need.
Social position and cancer rehabilitation referral.
Family background and attitudes at 22 predicting childlessness at 32; the arrangement is not the exposure.

IDENTIFIED. 'Old age pension and intergenerational living arrangements: a REGRESSION DISCONTINUITY DESIGN'. No abstract here, but the paired preprint below identifies it as China's 2009 rural pension. A clean discontinuity with the ARRANGEMENT as outcome -- design 6's shape. The population is elderly, so the configuration is the homonym's, but the instrument is exactly what the pre-launch arm lacks.
Maternal migrant status and child fostering in Nairobi settlements.
Fertility, contraception and intra-familial transfers in rural Malawi. C.3.c's old-age-security test.
Gender preferences and sex imbalances in Indonesia; bilateral kinship as the premise. D.2.c's.
EITC reform proposal; 'children living at home' is the eligibility condition.

Preprint of the preceding RD: China's 2009 rural pension, now covering 300 million people, against intergenerational co-residence under traditions of filial piety. Same instrument, and the setting is the extended arm's largest. Read both together.
